title: CPU reference implementations and GPU equivalence testing
subtitle: Every GPU metric has a plain-Rust CPU twin that defines it.

stats.label: lines of plain-Rust reference across thirteen modules
Rust integration tests, beside fifteen CUDA test files
older kernels kept with tests as regression baselines

lede: In the Inference Fabric's CUDA engine every metric and every search family has a CPU reference in plain Rust. The reference states the formula the obvious way and decides every edge case; the kernel is an implementation that must match it. A consistency check keeps the kernels, the references and the per-kernel lineage documentation in agreement for every kernel group. A metric that has no kernel yet stays on the CPU with its limit stated. The method is told in Every metric gets a CPU twin. The tolerances are part of the method.
quote: I do not trust a GPU kernel to define the number it computes.
evidence: Numerical testing of GPU kernels: a plain-Rust CPU reference of about 9,000 lines behind every metric, with a three-way check between kernel, reference and documentation.
Floating-point tolerance design: tolerances derived from single-precision reductions on 1,024-dimensional vectors, exact and byte-identical where search promises determinism.
Regression testing for GPU code: 32 Rust integration tests and 20 older kernels kept as baselines a rewrite is measured against.
author: Corey James
